title: HTML/CSS/JS DOM
summary: Framework-free web basics: semantic HTML for structure, external CSS for styling (selectors, specificity, the box model), and JavaScript that changes the page through the DOM: selecting elements, creating new ones, listening for events and stopping a form's default reload with preventDefault(). Step-by-step guide arrives when the lecture is published.
goal: Build a small page that responds to clicks and form submits using plain HTML, CSS and JavaScript.

steps.title: Read the two lessons
steps.detail: Read 'HTML & CSS' and 'JavaScript DOM' on the curriculum page. React does this DOM work for you in Myflix; this lecture shows what happens underneath.
steps.doneWhen: You can explain what the DOM is and why scripts use defer.

steps.title: Build a tiny to-do page
steps.detail: Make a scratch folder with index.html and app.js, then open index.html with Live Server. This uses the lesson's ideas: defer, addEventListener, createElement and preventDefault.
steps.code: // app.js const form = document.querySelector("#todo-form"); form.addEventListener("submit", (event) => { event.preventDefault(); const li = document.createElement("li"); li.textContent = form.task.value; document.querySelector("#list").appendChild(li); form.reset(); });
steps.doneWhen: Typing a task and pressing Add puts it in the list without the page reloading.

steps.title: Do the MDN events reading
steps.detail: Part II assigns MDN's Introduction to Events. Read: What is an event, addEventListener(), other listener mechanisms, event objects, preventing default behavior, and event bubbling.
steps.doneWhen: You can explain event bubbling in one sentence.

steps.title: Peek at Myflix's real DOM
steps.detail: Run Myflix (assignments/week-02/netflix, npm run dev), open Chrome DevTools > Elements and find a ShowCard. That HTML is what React built from your JSX.
steps.doneWhen: You found the HTML for one show card in the Elements panel.

concepts.meaning: The browser's tree of objects built from your HTML, which JavaScript can read and change.
Tags that describe meaning, like <nav>, <main> and <article>, not just looks.
The rule for which style wins when several match: ID beats class beats element.
A function that runs when something happens, like a click or a submit.
Stops the browser's built-in action, like reloading the page on form submit.
